summary.text: A joint distribution gives the probability that two or more random variables land in particular ranges or sets of values together.
With exactly two variables it is called bivariate, and from it you can work out each variable's marginal distribution and the conditional distributions.
In a table for two draws, each inner cell holds the probability of one combination of results, and all the cells together sum to 1.

facts.label: Two variables
facts.value: With only two random variables it is called bivariate

facts.label: Discrete case
facts.value: Described by a joint probability mass function

facts.label: Continuous case
facts.value: Described by a joint probability density function

facts.label: Table total
facts.value: The probabilities in all the cells sum to 1

facts.label: Independent draws
facts.value: A cell's probability is the product of each result's probability

items.prompt: Two independent draws are made, A and B. How do you get the probability of one particular combination of results, such as a specific result for each?

options.label: Add the probability of A's result to B's result
Multiply the probability of A's result by B's result
Take the larger of the two probabilities

items.explain: Because the draws are independent, the chance of a combination in one cell is the product of the chances of each result.

items.prompt: You list every possible combination of results from two draws and write the probability of each one. What should all those probabilities add up to?

options.label: One half, since there are two draws
It changes with how many draws there are

items.explain: Some combination is certain to occur, so the cell probabilities sum to 1, as with every probability distribution.

items.prompt: You roll a fair die. A is 1 when the roll is even, and B is 1 when the roll is prime (2, 3 or 5). Which roll makes both A and B equal 1?
items.explain: Even rolls are 2, 4 and 6; prime rolls are 2, 3 and 5. Only 2 is on both lists.

items.prompt: A teacher records each student's study time and test score together. She then asks only about scores, ignoring study time. What is the score distribution on its own called?
items.explain: A marginal distribution gives the probabilities for one variable with no reference to the values of the others.

items.prompt: Height and weight can each take any value in a range. Which tool describes their joint distribution?

options.label: A table of counts of whole numbers only

items.explain: For continuous variables the joint distribution is expressed with a joint probability density function; the mass function is for discrete variables.

items.prompt: A weather study records both temperature and rainfall for every day, treating them together. What is the name for a joint distribution of exactly two variables?
items.explain: With only two random variables the joint distribution is called bivariate, though the idea extends to any number.
